headline: Showers ease tonight, then foggy, breezy Tuesday and mostly dry Thursday and Friday.
summary: A cool dip in the high-altitude winds is moving in from the ocean and will push showers out of most lowland areas tonight. Behind it, the upper-level flow splits in two, keeping the next storm mostly to the south. A brief bulge of high pressure aloft should bring a dry Friday. Another system from the Gulf of Alaska is expected to send most of its energy toward Northern California. Monday is showery and the coolest in two weeks, with highs in the lower 50s and chilly lows tonight in the mid 30s to lower 40s. Tuesday is dry but foggy, with breezy east winds in the foothills that night. Showers return over the weekend, with snow levels dropping near the passes but little snow expected.
